deck.title: Impact of the Internet on Organisations & Society

front_blocks.md: Name the four positive impacts of the internet on organisations.

back_blocks.md: **Improved communication**, **access to global markets**, **access to a global workforce**, and changes in **how information is managed and used**.

cards.front_md: Name the four positive impacts of the internet on organisations.
cards.back_md: **Improved communication**, **access to global markets**, **access to a global workforce**, and changes in **how information is managed and used**.

front_blocks.md: Name four ways an organisation can communicate with its customers online.

back_blocks.md: Through **websites**, **email**, **instant messaging** and **social media**, easily and in **real time**.

cards.front_md: Name four ways an organisation can communicate with its customers online.
cards.back_md: Through **websites**, **email**, **instant messaging** and **social media**, easily and in **real time**.

front_blocks.md: Name three costs an organisation can reduce by selling products online.

back_blocks.md: **Overheads** such as rent, utilities and staff, **packaging**, and **postal charges**.

cards.front_md: Name three costs an organisation can reduce by selling products online.
cards.back_md: **Overheads** such as rent, utilities and staff, **packaging**, and **postal charges**.

front_blocks.md: How does the internet widen an organisation's access to a workforce?

back_blocks.md: Organisations can **find and hire the best talent regardless of location**, be **more selective** rather than limited to travelling distance, select employees from **different time zones**, and possibly **reduce costs** where wages are lower.

cards.front_md: How does the internet widen an organisation's access to a workforce?
cards.back_md: Organisations can **find and hire the best talent regardless of location**, be **more selective** rather than limited to travelling distance, select employees from **different time zones**, and possibly **reduce costs** where wages are lower.

front_blocks.md: Where does the big data organisations analyse come from?

back_blocks.md: From **smartphones**, **online applications**, **social media** and **payment systems**.

cards.front_md: Where does the big data organisations analyse come from?
cards.back_md: From **smartphones**, **online applications**, **social media** and **payment systems**.

back_blocks.md: Organisations analyse big data to find **patterns** of behaviour.

cards.back_md: Organisations analyse big data to find **patterns** of behaviour.

front_blocks.md: What two things does analysing big data allow an organisation to improve?

back_blocks.md: It allows them to **improve the customer experience** and **improve process efficiency**.

cards.front_md: What two things does analysing big data allow an organisation to improve?
cards.back_md: It allows them to **improve the customer experience** and **improve process efficiency**.

front_blocks.md: Name the two negative impacts of the internet on organisations.

back_blocks.md: **Security issues** and **greater competition**.

cards.front_md: Name the two negative impacts of the internet on organisations.
cards.back_md: **Security issues** and **greater competition**.

front_blocks.md: How was organisational data traditionally kept secure?

back_blocks.md: It was kept in a **secure central location** using physical safety measures such as **walls**, **locks**, **alarms** and **security guards**.

cards.front_md: How was organisational data traditionally kept secure?
cards.back_md: It was kept in a **secure central location** using physical safety measures such as **walls**, **locks**, **alarms** and **security guards**.

front_blocks.md: Name the three ways employees typically access secure organisational data remotely.

back_blocks.md: Through a **VPN** to remotely access data on servers, by **transferring a copy** of the data home via external storage or email, or by storing the data on **someone else's server** in the cloud.

cards.front_md: Name the three ways employees typically access secure organisational data remotely.
cards.back_md: Through a **VPN** to remotely access data on servers, by **transferring a copy** of the data home via external storage or email, or by storing the data on **someone else's server** in the cloud.

front_blocks.md: What prevents unauthorised users intercepting data being transferred on the internet?

back_blocks.md: **Encryption**.

cards.front_md: What prevents unauthorised users intercepting data being transferred on the internet?
cards.back_md: **Encryption**.

front_blocks.md: How does an organisation guard against employees revealing login details?

back_blocks.md: By having **policies** that ensure employees are **accountable for their actions**.

cards.front_md: How does an organisation guard against employees revealing login details?
cards.back_md: By having **policies** that ensure employees are **accountable for their actions**.

front_blocks.md: Why does the internet drive down prices for consumers?

back_blocks.md: Consumers can **buy from organisations globally** rather than only local ones, and this **extra competition** drives down prices.

cards.front_md: Why does the internet drive down prices for consumers?
cards.back_md: Consumers can **buy from organisations globally** rather than only local ones, and this **extra competition** drives down prices.

front_blocks.md: Name three industries put at risk by the internet, and what threatened each.

back_blocks.md: **Music and film rental** by online downloads and streaming, **record labels** because independent artists can release their own music online, **estate agents** by online advertising and virtual viewings, **newspaper publishers** by online news services, and **postal services** because messages and digital media can be sent instantly.

cards.front_md: Name three industries put at risk by the internet, and what threatened each.
cards.back_md: **Music and film rental** by online downloads and streaming, **record labels** because independent artists can release their own music online, **estate agents** by online advertising and virtual viewings, **newspaper publishers** by online news services, and **postal services** because messages and digital media can be sent instantly.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Before the internet, organisations competed globally for customers.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Traditionally organisations were only in competition with others in their **local area or country**; the internet opened competition up globally.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Before the internet, organisations competed globally for customers.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Traditionally organisations were only in competition with others in their **local area or country**; the internet opened competition up globally.

front_blocks.md: Name three forms of mass communication affected by less-restricted networks.

back_blocks.md: **Broadcasting**, **publishing** and **the internet**.

cards.front_md: Name three forms of mass communication affected by less-restricted networks.
cards.back_md: **Broadcasting**, **publishing** and **the internet**.

front_blocks.md: How did an individual get a message to the masses before the internet?

back_blocks.md: They would need to **persuade a media outlet to broadcast their message**, which made it **difficult to reach the masses**.

cards.front_md: How did an individual get a message to the masses before the internet?
cards.back_md: They would need to **persuade a media outlet to broadcast their message**, which made it **difficult to reach the masses**.

front_blocks.md: How have social media and video streaming changed who can broadcast a message?

back_blocks.md: They have given society a **platform to share their own messages to a global audience**.

cards.front_md: How have social media and video streaming changed who can broadcast a message?
cards.back_md: They have given society a **platform to share their own messages to a global audience**.

front_blocks.md: Who or what controls what online content a user sees?

back_blocks.md: **Moderators** and **service owners** control what can be published, and **algorithms** determine what watchers see based on their **browsing history and online activity**.

cards.front_md: Who or what controls what online content a user sees?
cards.back_md: **Moderators** and **service owners** control what can be published, and **algorithms** determine what watchers see based on their **browsing history and online activity**.

front_blocks.md: Why does paid promotion reach more people?

back_blocks.md: **Paid promotion will be seen by more users** than content from individuals who do not pay.

cards.front_md: Why does paid promotion reach more people?
cards.back_md: **Paid promotion will be seen by more users** than content from individuals who do not pay.

front_blocks.md: What has been lost from user-generated reference sites?

back_blocks.md: They have **removed the element of fact checking by experts or editors**, so users can contribute content that **may or may not be true**.

cards.front_md: What has been lost from user-generated reference sites?
cards.back_md: They have **removed the element of fact checking by experts or editors**, so users can contribute content that **may or may not be true**.

front_blocks.md: Give one negative impact of less-restricted networks on law enforcement.

back_blocks.md: Social media and video messaging services can be used to **organise illegal activities while avoiding police**.

cards.front_md: Give one negative impact of less-restricted networks on law enforcement.
cards.back_md: Social media and video messaging services can be used to **organise illegal activities while avoiding police**.

front_blocks.md: Give three positive impacts of less-restricted networks on law enforcement.

back_blocks.md: A network of **CCTV cameras** records illegal actions, **footage captured on social media** helps identify suspects, and social media is used to **organise events to support victims**.

cards.front_md: Give three positive impacts of less-restricted networks on law enforcement.
cards.back_md: A network of **CCTV cameras** records illegal actions, **footage captured on social media** helps identify suspects, and social media is used to **organise events to support victims**.

front_blocks.md: Define **the information gap**.

back_blocks.md: The information gap is the **divide created between people who have access to online information and those who do not**.

cards.front_md: Define **the information gap**.
cards.back_md: The information gap is the **divide created between people who have access to online information and those who do not**.

front_blocks.md: What does being information rich give a person?

back_blocks.md: **Good access to information**, which **improves their education** and helps **enable them to make decisions**.

cards.front_md: What does being information rich give a person?
cards.back_md: **Good access to information**, which **improves their education** and helps **enable them to make decisions**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The information gap was created by the internet.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The gap has existed **since television and radio were introduced**; the internet has **further widened** it.

**True or False?**

**False.**

front_blocks.md: Define **the digital divide**.

back_blocks.md: The digital divide is the **gap between people who have access to digital devices and the internet and people who do not**.

cards.front_md: Define **the digital divide**.
cards.back_md: The digital divide is the **gap between people who have access to digital devices and the internet and people who do not**.

front_blocks.md: Name four factors that affect a person's access to digital technology.

back_blocks.md: **Economy and infrastructure**, **location**, **politics**, **religion**, **disability** and **social** factors.

cards.front_md: Name four factors that affect a person's access to digital technology.
cards.back_md: **Economy and infrastructure**, **location**, **politics**, **religion**, **disability** and **social** factors.

front_blocks.md: How does a country's economy affect access to the internet?

back_blocks.md: Countries with a **strong economy can invest in infrastructure** that provides access, while countries with **emerging and developing economies may prioritise other needs** such as food and healthcare.

cards.front_md: How does a country's economy affect access to the internet?
cards.back_md: Countries with a **strong economy can invest in infrastructure** that provides access, while countries with **emerging and developing economies may prioritise other needs** such as food and healthcare.

front_blocks.md: How does location affect access to digital technology?

back_blocks.md: People who live in **remote locations** may be somewhere **wireless signals or cabling cannot reach**.

cards.front_md: How does location affect access to digital technology?
cards.back_md: People who live in **remote locations** may be somewhere **wireless signals or cabling cannot reach**.

front_blocks.md: Give two ways politics can restrict access to information.

back_blocks.md: **Government control** can mean **not allowing access to certain websites or content from other countries**, and **blocking access to satellites** to stop television and radio broadcasts because of cultural influences.

cards.front_md: Give two ways politics can restrict access to information.
cards.back_md: **Government control** can mean **not allowing access to certain websites or content from other countries**, and **blocking access to satellites** to stop television and radio broadcasts because of cultural influences.

cards.front_md: Why can disability contribute to the digital divide?

front_blocks.md: How have traditional ways of socialising changed?

back_blocks.md: Meeting in person and talking have been **replaced with an increased use of digital devices**.

cards.front_md: How have traditional ways of socialising changed?

front_blocks.md: Give one benefit of the way the internet has changed socialising.

back_blocks.md: The internet allows people to **connect with other people around the world**.

cards.front_md: Give one benefit of the way the internet has changed socialising.

front_blocks.md: Give two negative effects of using digital devices to socialise.

back_blocks.md: It can lead to **isolation** and **anxiety around meeting people in real life**.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Income is one **social** factor, but access is also affected by **economy and infrastructure**, **location**, **politics**, **religion** and **disability**.
